findings.issue: The reasons for /api/auth/password/forgot, /api/auth/otp/request and /api/auth/otp/verify say the paths are exempt from the gateway limiter and point to the backlog for abuse control. The javadoc of RateLimitWebFilter.java:26 says auth endpoints are skipped because 'auth-service keeps its own limiter'. A reader of the reviewed list could think these endpoints have no limit at all, so the reason names the wrong control.
findings.fix: Change these reasons to name the real control, for example 'skipped by the gateway limiter; auth-service enforces its own limiter'. The backlog item can stay to assert that coverage.

summary: Round 2 at 57e9c94 resolves all round-1 findings. MAJOR, path traversal starting from a public route: the contract now sends 8 raw, un-normalised anonymous probes and requires exactly 400 for each. They cover %2e%2e, ..;, %2E%2E, encoded slash and double-slash traversal out of /api/products, /api/sellers, /api/auth/login and /api/categories into /api/admin/**, /api/seller/** and /api/orders. It also requires 400 or 401 for /api/sellers/me/ and /api/sellers/me;x=1. So disabling the WebFlux firewall default would now fail the build. MINOR, method override and HEAD: ?_method=DELETE and X-HTTP-Method-Override on POST /api/products/1 must give 401, and so must HEAD /api/sellers/me. MINOR, rules that are neither public nor plain authenticated: they are now pinned to exactly {ANY /actuator/** DENY, ANY /api/admin/** ROLE[4 roles]}, so a new denyAll or a rule for an unknown role fails. A new requireSupportedMatcher also fails loudly on any rule shape other than a path rule before the final catch-all, which is a useful extra guard. MINOR, Q1 edge seller role rule and rate-limit coverage: both are recorded in .openforge/knowledge/backlog.md under F-20261119-17. MINOR, abusable public endpoints: their reasons now name the control. The RateLimitWebFilter claims for POST views, ad beacons and support chat match the source, where writes have their own budget and /api/auth/ is skipped. Nothing new is exposed: no src/main or build.gradle diff, and no new dependency. The 6-hour token lifetime comes from runtime-generated test-only keys. The new PROBE output prints only the method, path and status, never tokens. The only remaining point is a nit about the wording of the auth-endpoint reasons.
